title: Products
Business Loan
baseline: SME / Business Loans MiBank provides Micro Enterprise loans for existing small businesses. Loan amounts for Micro Enterprise Loans are from K200 through to K15,000. Business Loans are provided for the expansion of existing businesses and these Loans range from K15,000 upwards. MiBank has provided loans for all types of business activities across the 13 provinces in which it is located. These include street vending businesses and trade stores through to bakeries, fishing and transport. Agribusinesses is included and MiBank has funded chicken farms and the growing of cash crops such as cocoa, copra, coffee and oil palm. MiBank has also entered into various Credit Guarantee Schemes with a number of local district administrations in order to promote and develop micro enterprises and provide access to finance in the districts with a particular emphasis on equal access to finance for women. title: MiCash
baseline: MiCash is a Bank Account that is operated through a mobile phone attached to the Digicel network. The ability to execute financial transactions through a mobile device is commonly referred to as Mobile Money. It is estimated that 85% of Papua New Guineans do not have a Bank account, whereas many of these ‘unbanked’ citizens do have a mobile phone. In the developing world, Mobile Money deployments are occurring at a rapid rate to provide people in poor or rural areas with access to financial services. MiBank is the first licensed financial institution in Papua New Guinea to introduce Mobile Money. Press here for Fees Where can I open a MiCash account? A MiCash Account can be opened at any branch of MiBank or at any agent displaying the MiCash Account Opening Agent sign. What kind of transactions can I do on my phone with MiCash? MiCash enables you to buy goods and services, process bill payments, obtain air-time top up, send money transfers, do a balance check, and deposit or withdraw cash. Where can I deposit (cash in) or withdraw (cash out) from my MiCash account? At any Branch of MiBank or at any Agent displaying the MiCash Accepted Here sign. Can I have my pay go in to a MiCash Account? Yes every MiCash wallet has an associated Bank account number which you can provide to your paymaster. How is my MiCash account protected? Every customer will be provided with a Personal identification number (PIN) to operate their MiCash account. How can I find out more about MiCash? Please talk to our friendly staff at any branch of MiBank, or telephone our call centre on Digicel 16789 (free call). “If you’ve got a mobile you’ve got a bank” To Download the MiCash Application form please click below - MiCash

MiCash is a Bank Account that is operated through a mobile phone attached to the Digicel network.

The ability to execute financial transactions through a mobile device is commonly referred to as Mobile Money. It is estimated that 85% of Papua New Guineans do not have a Bank account, whereas many of these ‘unbanked’ citizens do have a mobile phone. In the developing world, Mobile Money deployments are occurring at a rapid rate to provide people in poor or rural areas with access to financial services. MiBank is the first licensed financial institution in Papua New Guinea to introduce Mobile Money.

Press here for Fees

Where can I open a MiCash account?
A MiCash Account can be opened at any branch of MiBank or at any agent displaying the MiCash Account Opening Agent sign.

What kind of transactions can I do on my phone with MiCash?
MiCash enables you to buy goods and services, process bill payments, obtain air-time top up, send money transfers, do a balance check, and deposit or withdraw cash.

Where can I deposit (cash in) or withdraw (cash out) from my MiCash account?

At any Branch of MiBank or at any Agent displaying the MiCash Accepted Here sign.

Can I have my pay go in to a MiCash Account?
Yes every MiCash wallet has an associated Bank account number which you can provide to your paymaster.

How is my MiCash account protected?
Every customer will be provided with a Personal identification number (PIN) to operate their MiCash account.

How can I find out more about MiCash?
Please talk to our friendly staff at any branch of MiBank, or telephone our call centre on Digicel 16789 (free call).

“If you’ve got a mobile you’ve got a bank”

title: Board of Directors
baseline: Board of Directors Trudi Egi, Chief Executive Officer Trudi Egi has had an illustrious career in the Banking Industry. He was previously with NDB and the PNG Institute of Banking & Business Management and holds an MBA from Torrens University Australia. Trudi is a key driver of rural development and digital financial services in MiBank. Peter Aitsi, Chairman Peter Aitsi is a senior business executive who recently led Credit Corporation Limited as its Group CEO. Prior to joining Credit Corp, Peter was the Country Manager for Newcrest Mining. Peter is also a former President of the Media Council of PNG, founding President of the Badili Club, and previously Deputy Chair of City Mission. He is the current Chairman of Transparency International and media company PNGFM. He is also a Director of Steamships Limited. Wavie Kendino, Director Wavie joined the Board in 2019 and is the Head of Legal at ANZ Bank in PNG. Wavie holds a Masters of Commercial Law from the University of Melbourne and is highly experienced in banking and finance, corporate and commercial law. Whilst previously with Dentons as a Senior Associate, Wavie assisted in advising financial institutions, the PNG Government, the Central Bank, state owned enterprises, corporates and NGOs on a range of transactions, projects and matters. Jason Mcilvena, Director Jason is the General Manager and Company Secretary of Kwila Corporation. Jason holds a Bachelor of Commerce majoring in Accounting, Law and Economics from Deakin University. Jason has had many years of experience in the Asia Pacific region including American Samoa, Fiji, Laos, New Zealand and the Solomon Islands. Jason is an FCPA and a member of the ANZIIF. Paul Nindipa, Director Paul is a Partner with the firm NKA Chartered Accountants. A past Treasurer of Transparency International, Paul holds a number of Board positions including Comrade Trustee Services limited and National Roads Authority. Paul is also a Council member of CPA Papua New Guinea and also member of both the PNG Institute of Directors and the Australian Institute of Company Directors. Paul chairs the Audit & Risk Board Sub-Committee for MiBank. Arthur Vera, Director Arthur Vera is a technology and communications specialist having spent a period of 24 years with Datec across a number of Pacific Island nations. Arthur was also involved with the establishment of bemobile in the Solomon Islands, and more recently is associated with Asia Pacific Communications Specialists, providing IT services for corporate clients. Arthur has served on various Boards including MTSL, BOC PNG, Trukai Industries, Marsh Insurance, Origin Energy and SVS. Ruth Kissam, Director Ruth is a community organizer and human rights activist who is passionately engaged with promoting human rights for women. Ruth has focused on addressing sorcery related violence in PNG. Ruth is an Obama Foundation Scholar and a member of the PNG Human Rights Commission. Previously Ruth had been involved in HIV and AIDS awareness and in 2018 was a recipient of the Westpac Outstanding Woman Award.

title: About Us
baseline: About Us MiBank is the registered trading name for Nationwide Microbank Limited, incorporated in Papua New Guinea. MiBank originated in 2004 as Microfinance project co-financed by Asian Development Bank, Australian Aid, and the Government of Papua New Guinea, under the then name of Wau Microbank. MiBank is licensed and regulated by the Central Bank, Bank of Papua New Guinea. The Bank delivers modern and affordable, savings, loans and insurance products, from a network of 12 branches and many agents across Papua New Guinea. MiBank is at the forefront of innovation, being the first licensed financial institution to deploy a Mobile Wallet in the South Pacific, called MiCash, and the first institution to introduce a Microinsurance product in Papua New Guinea called MiLife. MiBank prides itself on diversity and women's banking is a key focus area. The Bank empowers women and grassroots people generally through financial literacy training and access to its products and services. MiBank is the largest Microfinance institution in the South Pacific.

title: Privacy Policy
baseline: Privacy Policy At MiBank the privacy of your personal information is important to us. We value your trust, and aim to help you manage and build your wealth. We collect personal information (such as name, address and contact details) to provide you with products and services you request as well as information on other products and services offered by MiBank. The law may also require us to collect personal information. If you do not provide your personal information, we may not be able to provide you with all of our products and services. How your personal information is used Your personal information may be used by us to administer, monitor and evaluate products and services, gather, aggregate and report statistical information, assist you with any queries and take measures to detect and prevent fraud and other illegal activity. MiBank may also disclose relevant personal information to external organisations that help us provide services. We may disclose your personal information to recipients located in countries outside of Papua New Guinea. We may be required to disclose information by law and to report on prudential or risk management matters to regulators and related bodies. Access and Accuracy of your Personal Information You can seek access to the personal information we hold about you, subject to certain exceptions. If the information we hold about you is inaccurate, incomplete, or out of date, please inform us so we can correct it. If you provide us with incomplete or inaccurate information, we may not be able to provide you with the products or services you are seeking. You can also contact us to make a complaint about our handling of your personal information. If you have any questions or would like further information on our privacy and information handling practices, please call MiBank on +675 321 3811.

We collect personal information (such as name, address and contact details) to provide you with products and services you request as well as information on other products and services offered by MiBank. The law may also require us to collect personal information. If you do not provide your personal information, we may not be able to provide you with all of our products and services.

How your personal information is used
Your personal information may be used by us to administer, monitor and evaluate products and services, gather, aggregate and report statistical information, assist you with any queries and take measures to detect and prevent fraud and other illegal activity. MiBank may also disclose relevant personal information to external organisations that help us provide services. We may disclose your personal information to recipients located in countries outside of Papua New Guinea.

We may be required to disclose information by law and to report on prudential or risk management matters to regulators and related bodies.

Access and Accuracy of your Personal Information
You can seek access to the personal information we hold about you, subject to certain exceptions. If the information we hold about you is inaccurate, incomplete, or out of date, please inform us so we can correct it. If you provide us with incomplete or inaccurate information, we may not be able to provide you with the products or services you are seeking.

You can also contact us to make a complaint about our handling of your personal information.
If you have any questions or would like further information on our privacy and information handling practices, please call MiBank on +675 321 3811.

title: History
baseline: History of MiBank In 2000, the Asian Development Bank (ADB) carried out a study on the economy of PNG with the intention of providing financial assistance to support poverty alleviation of the Country. Based on the recommendations of the ADB report and with a goal of alleviating poverty, in 2002 the Government of PNG and ADB initiated the PNG-ADB Microfinance and Employment Project to address the financial needs of micro and small enterprises, subsistence farmers and poor households who were without financial services. As a major component of the Project, a micro banking pilot scheme was started in April 2004 in Wau under the Business Name of Wau Microbank. The policy making body for microfinance pilot project was the Project Steering Committee and the Bank was managed by the PNG Institute of Banking and Business Management who held the Certificate of Exemption. In February 2007, WMB was incorporated as a limited liability company under the Companies Act and all assets and liabilities of Wau Microbank were transferred to WMB Limited. In June 2008 BPNG withdrew the Certificate of Exemption and issued a banking licence to Nationwide Microbank Limited, the new name adopted to better reflect the proposed geographical scope of its operations. In 2013 the trading name of MiBank was registered and in 2020 MiBank acquired both PNG Microfinance Limited and the EsiLoan business from Kina Bank. MiBank now has 16 branches and more than Agents operating throughout Papua New Guinea

History of MiBank

In 2000, the Asian Development Bank (ADB) carried out a study on the economy of PNG with the intention of providing financial assistance to support poverty alleviation of the Country. Based on the recommendations of the ADB report and with a goal of alleviating poverty, in 2002 the Government of PNG and ADB initiated the PNG-ADB Microfinance and Employment Project to address the financial needs of micro and small enterprises, subsistence farmers and poor households who were without financial services. As a major component of the Project, a micro banking pilot scheme was started in April 2004 in Wau under the Business Name of Wau Microbank. The policy making body for microfinance pilot project was the Project Steering Committee and the Bank was managed by the PNG Institute of Banking and Business Management who held the Certificate of Exemption. In February 2007, WMB was incorporated as a limited liability company under the Companies Act and all assets and liabilities of Wau Microbank were transferred to WMB Limited. In June 2008 BPNG withdrew the Certificate of Exemption and issued a banking licence to Nationwide Microbank Limited, the new name adopted to better reflect the proposed geographical scope of its operations. In 2013 the trading name of MiBank was registered and in 2020 MiBank acquired both PNG Microfinance Limited and the EsiLoan business from Kina Bank. MiBank now has 16 branches and more than Agents operating throughout Papua New Guinea

html:
The MiBank Payroll Loan is designed to meet the needs of all Government Employees who are on Concept Payroll

- Minimum loan K200 to maximum of K5,000
- Minimum term of 5 fortnights through to maximum of 26

Eligibility Criteria

- Must be a Public Servant
- Must open a Passbook Account with MiBank
- Must be employed 12 months or more
- Must be on current Concept Payroll

Requirements

- Confirmation letter from Employer
- Two latest original Pay Slips
- Irrevocable Salary Deduction Authority (ISDA)
- Pay Variation Advice Form from Payroll (PVA)
- Copy of bank account statement where salary is credited
- Identification Card
